title: Palindrome Linked List
description:
# Palindrome Linked List

Given the `head` of a singly linked list, return `true` if the node values read the same from head to tail and from tail to head. Otherwise, return `false`.

Only the values are compared. Repeated values do not prove that a list is a palindrome; the mirrored positions must match all the way to the center.

Example arrays display values in `next` order; `[]` denotes an empty list (`null`). A node stores its value in `val` and its next node in `next`. Use node objects for list parameters and results as shown in the initial code.

## Example 1

**Input:** head = [1,2,2,1]
**Output:** true
**Explanation:** The values read as 1,2,2,1 in both directions.

## Example 2

**Input:** head = [1,2]
**Output:** false
**Explanation:** The first and last values differ.

## Constraints

*   The number of nodes in the list is in the range `[1, 10^5]`.
*   `0 <= Node.val <= 9`

tests.description: Single node is always a palindrome
Odd-length palindrome with one middle node
Longer even-length list with an inner mismatch
Repeated values are not enough when mirrored positions differ
Upper and lower allowed digit values
Longer odd palindrome with boundary zeros

solutions.name: Reverse Second Half and Restore
solutions.description:
## Approach

Use slow and fast pointers to find the end of the first half. Reverse the second half, compare the first half with the reversed second half, then reverse the second half again to restore the original list before returning.

## Key Insight

A singly linked list cannot be scanned backward, so reversing only the second half creates a forward traversal of the mirrored suffix. Restoring the suffix keeps the input list unchanged for callers.

## Complexity Analysis
- Time Complexity: O(n)
- Space Complexity: O(1)

solutions.name: Stack of First-Half Values
solutions.description:
## Approach

Move slow and fast pointers together. While fast advances two nodes, push each first-half value seen by slow onto a stack. If the list length is odd, skip the middle node, then compare the second half against stack pops.

## Key Insight

The stack stores the first half in reverse order, exactly matching the order needed to compare against the second half. This avoids mutating links, at the cost of extra memory.

## Complexity Analysis
- Time Complexity: O(n)
- Space Complexity: O(n)

solutions.name: Recursive Front Pointer
solutions.description:
## Approach

Use recursion to move a `right` pointer to the end of the list. During recursive unwinding, compare `right` with a `front` pointer that moves forward from the head.

## Key Insight

The call stack visits nodes from tail back to head during unwinding, so it supplies the backward traversal that a singly linked list does not have. In Java this is mainly a teaching route because very deep lists can overflow the call stack.

## Complexity Analysis
- Time Complexity: O(n)
- Space Complexity: O(n) recursion stack

solutions.name: Array Snapshot Two Pointers
solutions.description:
## Approach

Copy all node values into an array list. Then compare the value at the left index with the value at the right index while the two indices move toward the center.

## Key Insight

Once the linked-list values are in random-access storage, the problem becomes the ordinary two-pointer palindrome check used for arrays or strings. This baseline is simple and does not mutate the list.

## Complexity Analysis
- Time Complexity: O(n)
- Space Complexity: O(n)
